To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the expression of STAT1 and several phospho-STATs were differentially expressed in endocrine resistant breast cancer lines, 2) the STAT1 inhibitor EGEG and the STAT3 inhibitors Static and WP1066 inhibited the growth of endocrine-resistant MCF-7 lines, 3) STAT1 and STAT 3 were differentially expressed and regulated in primary breast cancers and matched axillary lymph nodes, 4) STAT1 expression was associated with distant metastasis-free

(i) STAT1 is over-expressed in endocrine-resistant MCF-7 variants and in lymph node metastases; (ii) STAT1 and STAT5 are predictive of distant metastases-free survival; and (iii) STAT3 is predictive of distant metastasess-free survival.

(1) STAT1 signaling is increased in endocrine-resistant breast cancers; (2) inhibition of STAT1 and/or STAT3 may be a useful treatment for breast cancer, particularly in endocrine-resistant tumors; (3) STAT3 signaling may be a useful biomarker for predicting response to endocrine therapy and survival in breast cancer.

identifying new molecular markers of endocrine resistance in breast cancer and developing new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of this disease.
